sentences.text:
The essential grievance of the Petitioner is as to the order of SLAO made on 14.06.2022, wherein it is inter alia observed as under:
"Now, even to the extent of 51 acres 07 guntas in Survey No.77 and 130 the claimant is unable to produce the documents, except those specifically mentioned above.

There are various persons whose names are forthcoming as per the preliminary and final notification and since there is a "cloud on the title" of the present claimant, this office is not the competent forum to adjudicate upon the title and rights of the claimant vis-a-vis the grantees by the State Government.

The applicant/claimant has to independently establish his rights and title over the notified lands of Byalakere village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk before an appropriate forum or competent authority.
As such, without expressing any opinion on the title or rights of the applicant/claimant I deem it appropriate to dispose the objection filed by the claimant.

2. Learned counsel for the Petitioner passionately argues that had his clients been given a reasonable opportunity to produce the documents in their custody or power, there would not have been difficulty for adjudging the title to the subject property and this opportunity having been denied, the impugned order is liable to be voided on the ground of violation of principles of natural justice.

3. Learned AGA on request having accepted notice for the Official Respondents opposes the Writ Petition contending that when there is a serious dispute as to the title to the subject land in respect of which entries in the name of others do avail in the records, the SLAO cannot adjudicate the same,
his Jurisdiction being limited in the scheme of the 1894 Act and therefore, the impugned order Mysore Venkataswamy Chettiar Trust vs State Of Karnataka on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192854942/
2 cannot be faltered.

sentences.text: He also points out that the Petitioner has got alternate & more efficacious remedy in terms of Apex Court decision in DHULABHAI VS. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH, AIR 1969 SC 78.

entities.text: DHULABHAI VS. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH, AIR 1969 SC 78
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So contending, he seeks dismissal of the Writ Petition.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the petition papers, this court is broadly in agreement with the submission of learned AGA and therefore, declines indulgence in the matter, as has made in umpteen number of such cases, reserving liberty to the Petitioner to approach the appropriate Civil Court for the adjudication of title dispute, in accordance with law.
In that regard, all contentions are kept open.
